claim: Arnold's metre label does not determine his stratum code. Over the 39,833 padas that carry both, predicting the stratum from the metre label alone is right 40.4% of the time against a 21.7% majority-class baseline, with normalised mutual information 0.306.
locator: rigveda/info/strata.json, sha256 484e657e32ab7304aece763c072a1fa75d4042ffc4513d1426ba248776e0ed75; 66 distinct metre labels against 10 stratum codes; computed by 04-AUDITS/rv-chronology-instruments.py, output m1-metre-by-stratum.tsv
notes: Runs against the obvious objection to any test that uses the strata, namely that Arnold derived them from metre and so they are a relabelling of it. They are not: metre leaves most of the stratum assignment unexplained. It does explain some, which is why the metrical control in Hellwig, Scarlata and Widmer 2021 is the right move.

claim: Arnold's strata are, however, heavily entangled with book identity. Book predicts stratum 51.2% of the time against a 25.5% baseline, Cramer's V = 0.471 on a 10x5 table (chi-square 9,357, 36 df). Book 3 has no Archaic stanza, book 4 no Archaic and no Cretic, book 7 no Archaic, book 8 no Cretic and book 6 no Strophic.
locator: strata.json cross-tabulated against book; 04-AUDITS/rv-arrangement.py, output m2-book-by-stratum.tsv
notes: 93.2% of hymns (958 of 1,028) carry a single stratum code across all their stanzas, which is the mechanism: Arnold classified hymns, and hymns cluster by book. Any test that reads a book effect and a stratum effect as two agreeing instruments is counting one thing twice. This sharpens PUR-020 and PUR-021 and is why the book-10 control in RCI-008 was necessary.

claim: All five late-addition instruments concentrate their marks in Arnold 1905's Popular stratum. Of the stanzas each marks, the share that Arnold 1905 calls Popular is: Grassmann 40.6% (3.16x the corpus rate), Oldenberg 69.7% (5.42x), Arnold 1897 86.8% (6.75x), Wuest 69.5% (5.41x), Witzel 56.5% (4.39x). The corpus rate is 12.9%.
notes: The enrichment is confined to Popular. Archaic is depleted for every instrument (0.05x to 1.09x) and so are Strophic, Cretic and Normal. These instruments corroborate Arnold at the late end of his sequence and say nothing whatever about the ordering of Archaic, Strophic, Cretic and Normal among themselves.

claim: The 31 hymns Oldenberg 1888 identified as appendices, as listed by Hellwig 2020, are enriched in Arnold's Popular stratum at 5.71x, closely matching the enrichment of the VedaWeb oldenberg column at 5.42x.
locator: Hellwig 2020, LT4HALA, footnote 6, citing Oldenberg 1888, 197-202 and 222-223; scored against strata.json by 04-AUDITS/rv-chronology-instruments.py
notes: Two independent transcriptions of Oldenberg 1888 reaching the same enrichment is a reproducibility check on the transcriptions, not a second instrument.

claim: That agreement is not the book-10 effect. Excluding book 10 entirely, the odds of a stanza being Popular given that a scholar marked it are: Grassmann 15.3, Oldenberg 69.2, Arnold 1897 206.5, Wuest 70.2, Witzel 32.5 (Fisher exact, one-sided, every p below 1e-140). Inside the family books 2-7 alone the odds ratios are 9.7, 59.4, 142.7, 56.2 and 47.6.
locator: 04-AUDITS/rv-arrangement.py, output m6-popular-enrichment-controlled.tsv; four domains - whole corpus, books 1-9, book 10 only, family books 2-7
notes: This is the control the result needed. Book 10 is 48.0% Popular (RCI-005 table), so an agreement driven entirely by book 10 would have been four instruments noticing one book. It is not: the association is stronger inside books 1-9 than over the whole corpus, because outside book 10 Popular is rare (5.9%) and the marks still find it.

claim: The five instruments are not mutually independent, and one pair is barely distinguishable: Wuest 1928 and Oldenberg agree on 641 stanzas out of 699 and 709 marked, Jaccard 0.836. Witzel 1995 agrees with each at Jaccard 0.48. Grassmann 1876-7 is the most nearly independent, Jaccard 0.19 to 0.25 against the others.
notes: Constitution step 5. Wuest 1928 cannot be counted as evidence separate from Oldenberg 1888 in this data: whatever Wuest did with style and chronology, the stanzas the VedaWeb layer records him marking are almost exactly Oldenberg's. Recorded as DEP-030. The count of usable non-Arnold instruments is therefore three, not four.

claim: Oldenberg's arrangement rule holds against the text. Within deity groups, adjacent hymns run from longer to shorter far more often than the reverse: 364 descents against 153 ascents using VedaWeb's group labels, and 216 against 56 using maximal runs of identical addressee, which uses no group label at all. Monte Carlo over 20,000 random within-group permutations returns p below 0.01 for every book under both segmentations.
locator: Rule as stated in Hellwig 2020 s.5.4 reporting Oldenberg 1888, 191-197 and 265; tested by 04-AUDITS/rv-arrangement.py against rigveda/info/addressees.json and hymn lengths from strata.json; output m8-arrangement-runs.tsv
notes: The rule is tested here against the corpus, not accepted on Oldenberg's authority. The label-free segmentation is the load-bearing one: VedaWeb's group labels are Koelligan's, and book 7's last group is labelled 'appendix', so that segmentation is not innocent of the theory being tested.

claim: Hymns that break the arrangement rule are the hymns earlier scholars judged late. Of 153 rule-breaking hymns, Grassmann 1876-7 marks 47.7% against 20.1% of the 767 compliant hymns, odds ratio 3.63, p = 6.5e-12.
notes: Grassmann is the one figure here for whom this is not circular. He published in 1876-7, twelve years before Oldenberg formulated the arrangement rule in 1888, so his marks cannot be an application of it. Oldenberg's own odds ratio of 15.4 on the same table is definitionally inflated, because violating the rule is how he identified appendices; it is reported in the output file and must not be cited as corroboration.

claim: The corroboration in RCI-006 and RCI-008 is real but it is not four independent measurements. Grassmann 1876-7 and Oldenberg 1888 both precede Arnold 1905, so the agreement cannot be those scholars following Arnold; it can be Arnold 1905 following them.
